data.name: Farras
data.gender_notes: Farras is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Farras is derived from the word for 'horses'. In Islamic history, horses were a symbol of power, strength, and speed. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) rode a horse during the Hijrah (Migration to Medina), making it an important part of Islamic history. Farras is a powerful and noble name, reflecting the courage and resilience of the early Muslims.
data.spiritual_meaning: Guiding others to hidden spiritual treasures.
data.etymology: Farras belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Horses.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farras total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: فرس
in_arabic.long_meaning: فرس هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الشديد السريع الجريء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة النمل آية 61: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَى وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا وَأَنَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالنَّاسِ مِنْ جِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكِيلَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَيَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَقْطُوعٍ وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَعْظَمُ الْحَاسِدِينَ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: أَضْحَكَ مَن قَرَأَ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ وَأَبْكَى مَن تَأَمَّلَ مَعْنَاهَا

in_english.name: Farras
in_english.long_meaning: The name Farras originates from Arabic roots, signifying a strong, swift, and courageous individual. It appears in Islamic tradition and Quranic context, embodying virtues of bravery and swiftness. Historically, it has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing desirable personality traits.

Such a name carries an aura of strength and power, reminiscent of the mighty steeds of the Islamic civilization. Horses were not just mounts but symbolized military might, liberty, and mobility, making the name Farras synonymous with enduring strength and valor.
